title: Teriyaki Chicken Casserole
text:
!! About

Casseroles are the great democratic dish — they don't really care if you can cook. Throw the pieces in a pan, send it to the oven, come back later. This one wraps the gloss-and-savor of teriyaki around a base of brown rice and stir-fry vegetables, and it has the particular American virtue of feeding a lot of people on a Wednesday night without anyone having to think about it.

The teriyaki sauce here is a real one — soy, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, thickened with cornstarch — not a shortcut from a bottle. Make extra and keep it in the fridge; it improves leftovers all week.

!! Ingredients

* 3/4 cup [[soy sauce]]
* 1/2 cup [[water]]
* 1/4 cup [[brown sugar]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[ground ginger]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[minced garlic]]
* 4 Tablespoons [[cornstarch]]
* 2 [[chicken breasts]]
* 1 (12 oz.) [[stir-fry vegetables]]
* 3 cups [[brown rice]]

!! Steps

# Preheat oven to 350° F.
# Spray a 9x13-inch baking pan with non-stick spray.
# Combine soy sauce, ½ cup water, brown sugar, ginger and garlic in a small saucepan and cover.
# Bring to a boil over medium heat.
# Remove lid and cook for one minute once boiling.
# Stir together the corn starch and 2 tablespoons of water in a separate dish until smooth.
# Once sauce is boiling, add mixture to the saucepan and stir to combine.
# Cook until the sauce starts to thicken, then remove from heat.
# Place the chicken breasts in the prepared pan.
# Pour one cup of the sauce over top of chicken.
# Place chicken in oven and bake 35 minutes or until cooked through.
# Remove from oven and shred chicken in the dish using two forks.
# Steam or cook the vegetables according to package directions.
# Add the cooked vegetables and rice to the casserole dish with the chicken.
# Add most of the remaining sauce, reserving a bit to drizzle over the top when serving.
# Gently toss everything together in the casserole dish until combined.
# Return to oven and cook 15 minutes.
# Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

title: Chicken Handi
text:
!! About

//Handi// means ''clay pot'' in Hindi and Urdu, and the dish is named for the vessel: a deep, round-bellied pot that holds heat slowly and lets the spices bloom into the meat without scorching. You don't need an actual handi — a heavy-bottomed pot will do the job — but the principle is the same. Time, low heat, and patience.

This is a long-cook chicken curry of the cream-and-yogurt school: deep-fried onions melted back into the sauce, garam masala bloomed in oil, dried fenugreek leaves crumbled in at the end for that characteristic faintly bitter, faintly maple aroma that signals ''this is going to be good''. Eat it with naan or rice and a cold lassi.

!! Ingredients

* 1.2 kg [[Chicken]]
* 5 thinly sliced [[Onion]]
* 2 finely chopped [[Tomatoes]]
* 8 cloves chopped [[Garlic]]
* 1 tbsp [[Ginger paste]]
* ¼ cup [[Vegetable oil]]
* 2 tsp [[Cumin seeds]]
* 3 tsp [[Coriander seeds]]
* 1 tsp [[Turmeric powder]]
* 1 tsp [[Chilli powder]]
* 2 [[Green chilli]]
* 1 cup [[Yogurt]]
* ¾ cup [[Cream]]
* 3 tsp Dried [[fenugreek]]
* 1 tsp [[Garam masala]]
* To taste [[Salt]]

!! Steps

# Take a large pot or wok and heat the oil in it.
# Once the oil is hot, add the sliced onion and fry until deep golden brown.
# Remove the onion to a plate and set aside.
# Add the chopped garlic to the same pot and sauté for a minute.
# Add the chopped tomatoes and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
# Return the fried onion to the pot and stir.
# Add ginger paste and sauté well.
# Add the cumin seeds, half of the coriander seeds, and chopped green chillies, and give a quick stir.
# Add the turmeric powder and red chilli powder and sauté the spices well for a couple of minutes.
# Add the chicken pieces, season with salt to taste, and cook covered on medium-low heat until almost cooked through, about 15 minutes.
# When the oil separates from the spices, add the beaten yogurt with the heat on its lowest setting so the yogurt doesn't split.
# Sprinkle in the remaining coriander seeds and add half of the dried fenugreek leaves, and mix well.
# Add the cream and mix to combine everything.
# Sprinkle the remaining kasuri methi and garam masala.

title: Tandoori chicken
text:
!! About

The deep red color of tandoori chicken comes traditionally from kashmiri chili and a long marinade in spiced yogurt — the yogurt's lactic acid tenderizes the meat while the spices coat every fiber. The name comes from the //tandoor//, the cylindrical clay oven that gets hot enough (somewhere north of 480°C) to char the outside of the chicken in minutes while the inside stays juicy.

Most home kitchens don't have a tandoor, and that's fine. A hot grill, or even a hot oven, will get you most of the way there — the magic is really in the marinade. Make this when the weather is good and you can cook outside; the smell of paprika and ginger and charring chicken is one of the great pleasures of summer.

!! Ingredients

* 2 Juice [[lemons]]
* 4 tsp [[paprika]]
* 2 finely chopped [[red onions]]
* 16 skinnless [[chicken thighs]]
* For brushing [[vegetable oil]]
* 300ml [[Greek yogurt]]
* large piece [[ginger]]
* 4 [[garlic clove]]
* ¾ tsp [[garam masala]]
* ¾ tsp [[ground cumin]]
* ½ tsp [[chilli powder]]
* ¼ tsp [[turmeric]]

!! Steps

# Mix the lemon juice with the paprika and red onions in a large shallow dish.
# Slash each chicken thigh three times, then turn them in the juice and set aside for 10 mins.
# Mix all of the marinade ingredients together and pour over the chicken.
# Give everything a good mix, then cover and chill for at least 1 hr.
# Heat the grill.
# Lift the chicken pieces onto a rack over a baking tray.
# Brush over a little oil.
# Grill for 8 mins on each side or until lightly charred and completely cooked through.

title: Vegetarian Shakshuka
text:
!! About

Shakshuka — eggs poached in a sauce of tomatoes, peppers and warm spices — has Maghrebi and Middle Eastern roots and has spread to nearly every brunch menu on earth, for good reason. It is forgiving, fast, beautiful in the pan, and uses things you already have. The eggs go in last, cracked into little wells in the sauce, and you cover the pan and wait until the whites just set while the yolks stay loose.

This is the simplest version: onion, pepper, tomatoes, cumin and paprika, a hit of cayenne, eggs, parsley, toast for dipping. Make it for one person on a quiet morning, or scale it up in a wide skillet and bring the whole pan to the table.

!! Ingredients

* 1/2 [[Red Onions]]
* 1/2 [[Red Pepper]]
* 400g [[Tomato]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Cumin]]
* 1/2 tsp [[Garlic Granules]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Cayenne Pepper]]
* 1 tsp [[Paprika]]
* 2 [[Egg]]
* Garnish [[Parsley]]
* Garnish [[Chilli Flakes]]
* 2 sliced [[Toast]]

!! Steps

# Fry onion and pepper together on medium heat until onion is soft
# Add garlic granules and cook for a minute
# Add chopped tomatoes and remaining spices, stir well
# Simmer for about 20 minutes
# Make indents in the sauce
# Crack an egg into each indent
# Once egg whites are cooked through, garnish

title: Vegetarian Chilli
text:
!! About

Sometimes dinner is //I have ten minutes and three things in the cupboard//. This is a recipe for that night.

Roasted vegetables (frozen or leftover), a tin of kidney beans, a tin of tomatoes, a packet of mixed grains heated in the microwave. Fifteen minutes start to finish. It is not glamorous and it is not trying to be — it is the kind of dinner that exists between proper meals, the bridge across a busy week. Hot sauce helps. So does a fried egg on top.

!! Ingredients

* 400g [[Roasted Vegetables]]
* 1 can [[Kidney Beans]]
* 1 can [[Chopped Tomatoes]]
* 1 Packet [[Mixed Grain]]

!! Steps

# Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
# Cook the vegetables in a casserole dish for 15 mins.
# Tip in the beans and tomatoes, season, and cook for another 10-15 mins until piping hot.

title: Vegetarian Casserole
text:
!! About

A casserole in the British sense — a pot of vegetables stewed slowly in tomato and stock until everything has gone soft and intermingled and the kitchen smells of thyme. Lentils stirred in at the end give it body and protein; the carrots, celery and peppers turn sweet from long cooking.

Serve over rice, mash, or quinoa. Keeps beautifully for several days in the fridge and is, if anything, better on day two. The kind of recipe to make on a Sunday and eat through the week.

!! Ingredients

* 1 [[Rapeseed Oil]]
* 1 [[Onion]]
* 3 cloves [[Garlic]]
* 1 tsp [[Paprika]]
* ½ tsp [[Cumin]]
* 1 tblsp [[Thyme]]
* 3 Medium [[Carrots]]
* 2 small stalks [[Celery]]
* 1 [[Red Pepper]]
* 1 [[Yellow Pepper]]
* 2 x 400g tins [[Tomato]]
* 250ml [[Vegetable Stock Cube]]
* 2 sliced [[Courgettes]]
* 2 sprigs [[Thyme]]
* 250g [[Lentils]]

!! Steps

# Heat the oil in a large, heavy-based pan.
# Add the onions and cook gently for 5 – 10 mins until softened.
# Add the garlic, spices, dried thyme, carrots, celery and peppers and cook for 5 minutes.
# Add the tomatoes, stock, courgettes and fresh thyme and cook for 20 - 25 minutes.
# Take out the thyme sprigs.
# Stir in the lentils and bring back to a simmer.

title: Vegan Lasagna
text:
!! About

Lasagna without dairy or meat sounds like it shouldn't work, and then you eat it and you forget about the //without//. The trick is building real flavor at every layer: lentils and vegetables stewed down until they're rich and slightly sweet; spinach blanched and tucked between sheets; a proper béchamel made with vegan butter, flour, and soya milk, sharpened with mustard and a splash of vinegar.

It takes a little while. But you assemble it once, bake it once, and you have dinner for several nights. A square of this with a green salad and a glass of red wine is a very civilized Tuesday.

!! Ingredients

* 1 cups [[green red lentils]]
* 1 [[Carrots]]
* 1 [[onion]]
* 1 small [[zucchini]]
* sprinking [[coriander]]
* 150g [[spinach]]
* 10 [[lasagne sheets]]
* 35g [[vegan butter]]
* 4 tablespoons [[flour]]
* 300ml [[soya milk]]
* 1.5 teaspoons [[mustard]]
* 1 teaspoon [[vinegar]]

!! Steps

# Preheat oven to 180°C.
# Boil vegetables for 5-7 minutes, until soft.
# Add lentils and bring to a gentle simmer, adding a stock cube if desired.
# Continue cooking and stirring until the lentils are soft, about 20 minutes.
# Blanch spinach leaves for a few minutes in a pan, then remove and set aside.
# Top up the pan with water, cook the lasagne sheets, then drain and set aside.
# Melt the butter and add the flour.
# Gradually add the soya milk along with the mustard and vinegar.
# Cook and stir until smooth.
# Assemble the lasagne in a baking dish.
# Bake in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes.

title: Vegan Chocolate Cake
text:
!! About

Vegan baking has come a long way from the dense, virtuous bricks of decades past. This cake is proof: cocoa-dark, tender, properly sweet, made with flax eggs in place of regular ones and almond milk instead of dairy. The boiling water at the end is the trick — it blooms the cocoa and gives the crumb a moist, almost fudgy quality.

Mix everything in one bowl. Bake. Decorate with melted vegan chocolate. Nobody at the table will be checking your ingredient list.

!! Ingredients

* 1 1/4 cup [[Self-raising Flour]]
* 1/2 cup [[coco sugar]]
* 1/3 cup raw [[cacao]]
* 1 tsp [[baking powder]]
* 2 [[flax eggs]]
* 1/2 cup [[almond milk]]
* 1 tsp [[vanilla]]
* 1/2 cup boiling [[water]]

!! Steps

# Mix all dry ingredients with wet ingredients and blend altogether.
# Bake for 45 minutes at 180 degrees.
# Decorate with melted vegan chocolate.

title: Vegan banh mi
text:
!! About

//Bánh mì// is the great Vietnamese sandwich — a legacy of French colonial baguettes meeting Vietnamese herbs, pickled vegetables and bright, sharp flavors. The classic has pâté and pork; this version swaps in tempeh and hummus and loses none of what makes the sandwich great: crunch, acid, freshness, heat.

Quick-pickle the shredded vegetables in vinegar and sugar while you toast the bread. Spread hummus thickly, layer the tempeh, pile on the pickles, tuck in handfuls of coriander and mint. Hot sauce to taste. Eat over a plate, because it will fall apart, and that's the point.

!! Ingredients

* 150g [[Raw Vegetables]]
* 3  tablespoons [[Vegan White Wine Vinegar]]
* 1 tsp [[Golden Caster Sugar]]
* 1 large [[Baguette]]
* 100g [[Hummus]]
* 175g [[Tempeh]]
* Handful [[Coriander]]
* Handful [[Mint]]
* To serve [[Hotsauce]]

!! Steps

# Put the shredded veg in a bowl and add the vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt.
# Toss everything together, then set aside to pickle quickly.
# Heat oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
# Cut the baguette into four, then slice each piece horizontally in half.
# Put the baguette pieces in the oven for 5 mins until lightly toasted and warm.
# Spread each piece with a layer of hummus.
# Top four pieces with the tempeh slices.
# Pile the pickled veg on top.
# Sprinkle over the herbs and squeeze over some hot sauce.
# Top with the other baguette pieces.

title: Turkish lahmacun
text:
!! About

//Lahmacun// is sometimes called Turkish pizza, which sells it short. It's its own thing — a thin, almost cracker-crisp round of dough spread with a paste of ground meat, tomato, onion, parsley and warm spices, baked very fast in a very hot oven. You roll it up around fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon and eat it with your hands.

This recipe makes the dough from scratch, which is the right way; the fast-action yeast keeps it manageable on a weeknight. The topping is mostly chopping. Get the oven as hot as it will go, and let each lahmacun cook only a few minutes — they should be tender enough to roll, not stiff.

!! Ingredients

* 500g [[Strong white bread flour]]
* 10g [[Fast action yeast]]
* Sprinkling [[Corn Flour]]
* 2 [[Tomato]]
* 2 [[Green Chilli]]
* 4 Chopped [[Spring Onions]]
* Bunch [[Parsley]]
* 250g [[Ground Beef]]
* 2 tsp [[Chilli Flakes]]
* Pinch [[Ground Cumin]]
* 1 tsp [[Allspice]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Olive Oil]]
* 1/2 [[Lemon]]
* 1 [[Red Onions]]

!! Steps

# Sift the flour into a large bowl, make a well in the middle and sprinkle in the yeast.
# Pour 125ml water over the yeast, then flick flour over the liquid to create a layer.
# Cover and leave to rise in a warm place for 15 mins until cracks appear on the surface of that layer.
# Use your hands to mix in 250ml more water along with 1 tsp salt and knead the dough for about 10 mins until elastic and no longer sticky, adding a little more flour if needed.
# Cover and leave to rise again in a warm place for 30 mins until doubled in size.
# Heat the oven to as high as it will go (about 240C/220C fan/gas 9).
# Sprinkle one or two baking trays thinly with cornmeal.
# Pour boiling water from the kettle over the tomatoes, leave to stand briefly, then drain and slip off the skins.
# Cut the tomatoes in half, cut out the stalks, scoop out the seeds and discard, then chop the flesh.
# Halve the chillies lengthways, cut out the stalks, seeds and white inner membrane, then rinse.
# Cut the chillies lengthwise into fine strips, then crosswise into fine dice.
# Put the tomatoes, chillies, spring onions, finely chopped parsley, beef mince, spices, 1 tsp salt and ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper into a bowl and mix well.
# Take the dough and knead it briefly, then divide into four pieces and shape each into a ball.
# Roll each ball into a thin circle and place on the prepared baking trays.
# Spread each with a thin layer of the meat mixture.
# Bake each flatbread for 10-15 mins until the edges begin to darken.
# After removing from the oven, sprinkle the lahmacun with the roughly chopped parsley and sliced onion, then squeeze over a few drops of lemon juice.

title: Algerian Carrots
text:
!! About

A North African side dish that turns the humble carrot into something interesting. Steamed until just tender, then warmed in olive oil with cumin, cinnamon, garlic, thyme and a bay leaf — the spice profile is unmistakably Mediterranean-meets-Maghreb, sweet and savory at once.

Serves well alongside grilled meats, couscous, or a tagine. Equally good cold the next day, dressed with a little extra lemon juice and eaten straight from the fridge.

!! Ingredients

* 1 1/2 cup [[Water]]
* 2 Lbs [[Carrots]]
* 5 tablespoons [[Olive Oil]]
* 1 tsp [[Salt]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Black Pepper]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Ground Cinnamon]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Ground Cumin]]
* 3 Cloves Crushed [[Garlic]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Thyme]]
* 1 [[Bay Leaf]]
* 1 tsp [[Lemon Juice]]

!! Steps

# Place a steamer insert into a saucepan and fill with 1 1/2 cups of water, or just below the bottom of the steamer.
# Cover and bring the water to a boil over high heat.
# Add the sliced carrots, reduce the heat to medium, and cover the pan again.
# Steam until tender but not mushy, 4 to 6 minutes depending on the thickness of the slices.
# Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking liquid.
# Heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat.
# Reduce the heat to low and stir in the salt, pepper, cinnamon, cumin, garlic, and thyme.
# Cook the spices and garlic, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 10 minutes.
# Add the 1/2 cup reserved cooking liquid and the bay leaf, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
# Stir in the carrots, tossing well to coat with the spice mixture, and cook until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes.
# Sprinkle with lemon juice and remove the bay leaf before serving.

title: Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce (photo)
Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce
photo: Falafel Pita Sandwich with Tahini Sauce (photo)
text:
!! About

Falafel — fried chickpea balls — are one of the great street foods of the Levant, and a falafel pita is the platonic form of the casual lunch: crunchy, creamy, fresh, hot and cold all at once. This is a quick assembly version, using ready-made falafel, but the components matter:

* Tahini sauce, thinned with water and brightened with lemon and garlic
* Crisp lettuce, ripe tomato, cucumber, dill pickle, raw red onion
* A spoonful of harissa for heat

Warm the pita just enough that it folds without cracking, and eat it standing up. The drips are part of the experience.

!! Ingredients

* 12 [[Falafel]]
* 1/4 cup [[Tahini]]
* 1/4 cup [[Water]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Lemon Juice]]
* 2 cloves [[Garlic]]
* 1/4 tsp [[Paprika]]
* 6 [[Pita Bread]]
* 1 [[Lettuce]]
* 1 [[Tomato]]
* 1/2 [[Cucumber]]
* 1 [[Dill Pickles]]
* 1/4 [[Red Onions]]
* 3 tsp [[Harissa Spice]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
# Place falafel on a baking sheet.
# Bake until heated through, 8 to 10 minutes.
# While falafel bake, whisk tahini, water, lemon juice, garlic, and paprika together in a bowl.
# Cut about 1 inch from the top of each pita to form a pocket.
# Add 2 falafel to each pita with equal amounts lettuce, tomato, cucumber, pickle, and red onion.
# Drizzle each with about 1 tablespoon tahini sauce and some harissa.

title: Rogaliki (Polish Croissant Cookies)
text:
!! About

//Rogaliki// are little Polish crescent cookies — flaky, tender, rich with butter and cream cheese, rolled around a dab of jam and dusted with powdered sugar. They are what your Polish grandmother served on a doily-lined plate when company came over, and they are what you should make when you want to feel briefly like someone's Polish grandmother.

The dough is unusual — half pastry, half cookie — and needs a short rest in the freezer before rolling. Use whatever jam you have. Apricot is traditional; raspberry, plum, or strong-flavored preserves all work beautifully.

!! Ingredients

* 1 cup [[Butter]]
* 3 [[Egg Yolks]]
* 8 oz [[Cream Cheese]]
* 1 tsp [[Baking Powder]]
* 3 cups [[Flour]]
* 1 Jar [[Jam]]

!! Steps

# In a medium bowl mix egg yolks, philly cheese and baking powder using a hand held mixer.
# Carefully start adding the flour.
# When the mixture will not be mixing well and will look like wood chips, put away the blending mixer and using your hands knead the dough.
# Create a roll and cover in foil.
# Freeze for 15 minutes.
# Preheat the oven to 375.
# Take the dough out and separate into two.
# Roll and cut out 3 inch triangles, making as many as you can.
# On the centre of each put a small spoon of jam.
# Roll them into a croissant shape.
# Place the croissants onto a greased cookie sheet.
# Bake for 10-12 minutes or until golden.
# Repeat with the rest of the dough.
# When you take them out, put aside and sprinkle with powdered sugar on top.

title: Carrot Cake
text:
!! About

Carrot cake's appeal is hard to explain to anyone who hasn't had a good one. //A vegetable, in a cake?// Yes. The carrots melt in during baking and leave only their sweetness and moisture behind, and what you get is a cake that's deeply spiced with cinnamon, dotted with walnuts, and capable of staying tender for days.

Top with cream cheese frosting — there is no other correct topping. Carrot cake without cream cheese frosting is just spice loaf, and life is too short for spice loaf.

!! Ingredients

* 450ml [[Vegetable Oil]]
* 400g [[Plain Flour]]
* 2 tsp [[Bicarbonate Of Soda]]
* 550ml [[Sugar]]
* 5 [[Eggs]]
* ½ tsp [[Salt]]
* 2 tsp [[Cinnamon]]
* 500g grated [[Carrots]]
* 150g [[Walnuts]]
* 200g [[Cream Cheese]]
* 150g [[Caster Sugar]]
* 100g [[Butter]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 160C/325F/Gas 3.
# Grease and line a 26cm/10in springform cake tin.
# Mix all of the ingredients for the carrot cake, except the carrots and walnuts, together in a bowl until well combined.
# Stir in the carrots and walnuts.
# Spoon the mixture into the cake tin and bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, or until a skewer inserted into the middle comes out clean.
# Remove the cake from the oven and set aside to cool for 10 minutes.
# Carefully remove the cake from the tin and set aside to cool completely on a cooling rack.
# Beat the cream cheese, caster sugar and butter together in a bowl until fluffy.
# Spread the icing over the top of the cake with a palette knife.

title: Pistachio Kunafa Chocolate Cake and Cupcakes (photo)
Pistachio Kunafa Chocolate Cake and Cupcakes
photo: Pistachio Kunafa Chocolate Cake and Cupcakes (photo)
text:
!! About

This is an ambitious dessert — a layered chocolate cake with homemade pistachio paste, sevaiyan (toasted vermicelli), and a chocolate-malai topping that nods to //kunafa//, the shredded-pastry sweet beloved across the Levant and Gulf. It crosses borders cheerfully: Oreos in the cake batter, ghee for the vermicelli, dark chocolate over the top.

It is fiddly. Several components, several steps, a fair bit of waiting. But the result is something genuinely unusual — a dessert that tastes like multiple traditions argued politely and arrived at consensus.

!! Ingredients

* 6 tablespoons [[White Chocolate]]
* 1 cup [[Unsalted Pistachio]]
* 3  tablespoons [[Condensed Milk]]
* 5 tablespoons [[Milk]]
* 25 [[Oreo Cream Biscuits]]
* 1/2 cup [[Milk]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Baking Powder]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Vinegar]]
* 1 pinch [[Salt]]
* 150g [[Sevaiiya]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Ghee]]
* 120ml [[Dark Chocolate]]
* 4 tablespoons [[Malai]]

!! Steps

# Ready all the cake ingredients.
# Powder the oreo biscuits, add a pinch of salt and warm milk as needed, and make a cake batter.
# Add in baking powder and vinegar and mix.
# Grease a loose bottomed tin.
# Pour a 1cm thick layer of the batter.
# Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C for 7-8 minutes or until the knife comes out clean.
# Cool on a wire rack.
# Ready all the pistachio paste ingredients.
# Slightly melt white chocolate on a double boiler.
# Coarsely powder the pistachio in a mixer.
# Add in condensed milk.
# Add in slightly warmed and slightly melted white chocolate and milk as required and crush to a smooth paste.
# In a kadhaai, take ghee and roast the sevaiiya on slow gas, stirring until a pleasant roasted aroma releases.
# Cool the kunafa.
# Add in the homemade pistachio paste and mix well.
# Spread a 2cm layer of kunafa on the cooled chocolate cake.
# Melt dark chocolate and strained malai and prepare the chocolate ganache.
# Cool and pour the ganache on the kunafa layer.
# Garnish with chopped pistachio and silver balls.
# Keep in fridge for 2-3 hours.
# Unmould the cake.

title: Salted Caramel Cheescake
text:
!! About

Cheesecake plus salted caramel plus pretzels plus toffee popcorn equals the most American dessert of all time, despite this version being made (perfectly) in a British kitchen. Sweet meets salty, soft meets crunchy, every bite slightly different from the last.

The base is a mixture of digestive biscuits and crushed pretzels — that's where the salty-sweet starts. The filling is a no-bake mixture of cream cheese, double cream, icing sugar and caramel sauce, with a generous pinch of sea salt. The top gets more caramel, more pretzels, more popcorn. It's not subtle. It's not trying to be.

!! Ingredients

* 250g [[Digestive Biscuits]]
* 75g [[Pretzels]]
* 135g [[Butter]]
* 450g [[Cream Cheese]]
* 1tsp [[Vanilla Extract]]
* 100g [[Icing Sugar]]
* 150g [[Caramel]]
* 1tsp [[Sea Salt]]
* 300ml [[Double Cream]]
* drizzle [[Caramel Sauce]]
* Top [[Toffee Popcorn]]
* Top [[Pretzels]]

!! Steps

# Blitz the biscuits and pretzels in a food processor.
# Mix the blitzed biscuits with the melted butter.
# Spread the mixture on the bottom of an 8″/20cm deep springform tin and press down firmly.
# Leave to set in the fridge while you make the filling.
# Whisk together the cream cheese, vanilla, and icing sugar until smooth.
# Add the caramel and whisk again until smooth and lump free.
# Pour in the double cream and salt flakes and continue to whisk until very thick and mousse-like, up to 5 minutes.
# Spread the filling over the biscuit base.
# Leave to set in the fridge overnight.
# Remove the cheesecake from the tin carefully.

title: Walnut, date & honey cake
text:
!! About

There is a particular kind of cake that doesn't announce itself. It doesn't need frosting or candles or a cake stand — it sits on a plate, sliced thick, perhaps next to a glass of strong tea, and quietly insists you have another piece. This is one of those.

The combination of walnuts, dates, and honey runs deep through Turkish and broader Middle Eastern baking, where dates have been cultivated for thousands of years and honey predates written history as a sweetener. What makes this particular cake feel modern is the banana, which keeps everything moist for days, and the muscovado sugar, which lends a faintly molasses-dark depth. Cinnamon ties it all together.

It is the kind of cake to make on a Sunday afternoon when the light is going soft and you want the kitchen to smell like something. Wrap a slice in waxed paper for someone's lunchbox. Set the rest on the counter under a tea towel, and watch how quickly it disappears.

!! Ingredients

* 225g [[Self-raising Flour]]
* 1/2 teaspoon [[Ground Cinnamon]]
* 175g [[Butter]]
* 100g [[Muscovado Sugar]]
* 3  tablespoons [[Clear Honey]]
* 2 Beaten [[Egg]]
* 2 medium [[Banana]]
* 100g [[Stoned Dates]]
* 50g [[Walnuts]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 160C/Gas 3/fan oven 140C.
# Line the base and long sides of a 900g/2lb loaf tin with greaseproof paper, buttering the tin and paper.
# Tip the flour, cinnamon, butter, sugar, 2 tablespoons of the honey and the eggs into a large mixing bowl.
# Mash the bananas and chop the dates (kitchen scissors are easiest for this) and add to the bowl.
# Beat the mixture for 2-3 minutes, using a wooden spoon or hand-held mixer, until well blended.
# Spoon into the prepared tin and level the top.
# Scatter the walnut pieces over.
# Bake for 1 hour, then lightly press the top – it will feel firm if cooked. If not, bake for a further 10 minutes.
# Cool for 15 minutes, then lift out of the tin using the paper.
# When cold, drizzle the remaining honey over.
# Cut into thick slices.

title: Baklava with spiced nuts, ricotta & chocolate (photo)
Baklava with spiced nuts, ricotta & chocolate
photo: Baklava with spiced nuts, ricotta & chocolate (photo)
text:
!! About

//Baklava// — paper-thin filo, melted butter, sugar syrup, nuts — is one of the great achievements of the Ottoman kitchen. It traveled across an empire and settled into a thousand local versions: pistachio-heavy in Gaziantep, walnut-forward in the Balkans, drowned in honey in Greece.

This is a more modern interpretation: walnuts, pecans, almonds, ricotta sweetened with citrus zest and vanilla, plus dark chocolate. The ricotta is the unusual move — it lightens the filling and adds a creamy contrast to the crunch. Cardamom and cinnamon provide the warm spice. The syrup-soaking at the end is non-negotiable.

!! Ingredients

* 500g [[Sugar]]
* To taste [[Lemon Juice]]
* 300g [[Walnuts]]
* 200g [[Pecan Nuts]]
* 100g [[Almonds]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Ground Cinnamon]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Ground Cardomom]]
* 500g [[Ricotta]]
* Zest of 1 [[Lemon]]
* Zest of 1 [[Orange]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Vanilla Bean Paste]]
* 250g [[Unsalted Butter]]
* 500g [[Filo Pastry]]
* 100g [[Ground Pistachios]]

!! Steps

# Tip the sugar into a large saucepan with 650ml water and stir over a low heat until the sugar has dissolved.
# Turn up the heat and bring to the boil.
# Reduce the heat to a simmer and cook for 15 mins.
# Squeeze in a few drops of lemon juice and simmer for a further 5 mins.
# Remove from the heat and leave to cool.
# Melt the butter in a small pan over a low heat for 5 mins, skimming and discarding any froth that rises to the surface.
# Crush all of the nuts in a pestle and mortar, or blitz in a food processor to a mixture of finely ground nuts with a few chunky pieces.
# Tip into a bowl, stir through the spices and set aside.
# In a separate bowl, mix the ricotta with the lemon and orange zests and vanilla.
# Heat the oven to 180C/160C fan/gas 4.
# Brush the bottom of a large baking tray (about 35 x 47cm) with some of the melted butter.
# Working with one sheet of filo at a time, covering the rest with a damp tea towel to prevent it drying out, lay the sheet on a board with one of the short ends facing you.
# Sprinkle 30g of the nut mixture evenly over the whole sheet.
# Spoon 1 tbsp of the ricotta mixture across the end closest to you.
# Fold this end over to enclose the filling.
# Lay a long, thin skewer next to the folded edge and roll the pastry around it to create a long roll.
# While holding one end of the skewer, gently scrunch the filo roll like an accordion and carefully push it off the skewer and onto the prepared tray.
# Repeat with the rest of the filo and fillings to make about 12 rolls.
# Cut each roll into four to make 48 large baklava, or eight to make 96 mini.
# Brush with the remaining melted butter.
# Bake for 20-25 mins until evenly golden, turning the tray around halfway through.
# While still hot, immediately pour over 5-6 ladlefuls of the syrup.
# Set aside to cool and absorb.
# Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of simmering water, ensuring the bowl doesn't touch the water, or in the microwave in short bursts.
# Drizzle over the cooled baklava and sprinkle with the ground pistachios.

title: Cashew Ghoriba Biscuits
text:
!! About

//Ghoriba// (or //ghribia//, depending on which side of the Maghreb you're on) is a family of North African shortbread cookies — crumbly, lightly sweet, often perfumed with orange blossom water. This Tunisian version is built on cashews and egg yolks rather than flour and butter, which makes them naturally gluten-free and gives them a chewy-tender texture closer to a French //macaron// than a shortbread.

Each cookie gets an almond pressed into its center, like a small full stop. They're traditionally served with mint tea, and they keep well for several days in a tin if you can manage not to eat them all the first afternoon.

!! Ingredients

* 250g [[Cashew Nuts]]
* 100g [[Icing Sugar]]
* 2 [[Egg Yolks]]
* 2 tbs [[Orange Blossom Water]]
* To Glaze [[Icing Sugar]]
* 100g [[Almonds]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 180 C / Gas 4.
# Line a baking tray with greaseproof paper.
# In a bowl, mix the cashews and icing sugar.
# Add the egg yolks and orange blossom water and mix to a smooth homogeneous paste.
# Take lumps of the cashew paste and shape into small balls.
# Roll the balls in icing sugar and transfer to the baking tray.
# Push an almond in the centre of each ghribia.
# Bake until the biscuits are lightly golden, about 20 minutes, keeping an eye on them as they burn quickly.

title: Sesame Cucumber Salad
text:
!! About

The Sichuan smashed cucumber — pai huang gua — is probably the most famous member of this family, but the basic idea travels widely across China and East Asia: cucumbers, salt, a sharp dressing, sesame.

This is a quiet, adaptable version. Peel the cucumbers, cut them into chunks, salt them lightly, dress with sesame oil, rice vinegar, chili flakes. Toasted sesame seeds on top. It's a five-minute side that goes with almost anything — grilled meat, dumplings, noodles, rice. Make it just before you sit down, because the cucumbers weep quickly and you want them still crunchy.

!! Ingredients

* 2 medium [[Cucumber]]
* 1/2 tsp [[Salt]]
* 2 tsp [[Sesame Seed Oil]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Rice Vinegar]]
* 6 [[Basil Leaves]]
* 1/2 tsp [[Red Chilli Flakes]]
* 2 tsp [[Sesame Seed]]

!! Steps

# Peel the cucumbers.
# Cut them into quarters, lengthwise.
# If the seeds are bitter, scrape out the seeds and discard.
# Cut the cucumbers crosswise into 1/2-inch thick pieces.
# Place cucumbers into a serving bowl.
# Sprinkle with salt.
# Toss with sesame oil, seasoned rice vinegar, basil (if using), and chili flakes.
# Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds if using.

title: Warm roast asparagus salad
text:
!! About

Asparagus and bacon were made for each other. The asparagus goes salty-sweet under the heat; the bacon, rolled into tight little spirals and roasted alongside, releases its fat over everything; tomatoes burst and add acidity; honey lacquers the bacon at the end.

Tossed with new potatoes and rocket and finished with a sharp mustard vinaigrette, this becomes a substantial warm salad — the kind of thing you eat at lunch in the garden in late spring, when asparagus season is brief and you want to put it in everything.

!! Ingredients

* 500g [[Asparagus]]
* 2 tbsp [[Red Wine Vinegar]]
* 4 [[Tomato]]
* 1 tbsp [[Extra Virgin Olive Oil]]
* 12 [[Streaky Bacon]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Clear Honey]]
* 16 [[Jersey Royal Potatoes]]
* 2 tblsp [[Extra Virgin Olive Oil]]
* 1 teaspoon [[Dijon Mustard]]
* 100g [[Rocket]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 200C/Gas 6/fan 180C.
# Snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and discard.
# Arrange the asparagus in a single layer in a baking tray with sides.
# Cut the tomatoes in half widthways, nestle them in with the asparagus, season with sea salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil.
# Roll each bacon rasher into a tight roll (if large, first cut in half crosswise), and arrange in the tray.
# Drizzle the bacon rolls with the honey and bake for 20 minutes until the tomatoes are soft and the bacon is crisp.
# Boil the potatoes until tender.
# Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, mustard, some sea salt and pepper in a large bowl until blended.
# Toss the rocket or spinach leaves in half of the dressing, and arrange on a large serving platter.
# Drain the potatoes and cut in half.
# Gently toss them in the rest of the dressing, and arrange on the platter with the asparagus.
# Tuck in the tomatoes and bacon.

title: Honey Teriyaki Salmon
text:
!! About

Salmon takes to teriyaki almost suspiciously well — the rich, fatty fish meeting the salty-sweet glaze in a way that feels like both ingredients have been waiting for each other. This recipe is small, fast, and built around a homemade glaze of soy, sake, and honey rather than anything bottled.

Pan-fry the salmon until just cooked, letting the glaze reduce and lacquer the surface. Sesame seeds on top. Steamed rice underneath. A weeknight dinner that punches well above its effort level.

!! Ingredients

* 1 lb [[Salmon]]
* 1 tablespoon [[Olive oil]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Soy Sauce]]
* 2 tablespoons [[Sake]]
* 4 tablespoons [[Sesame Seed]]

!! Steps

# Mix all the ingredients in the Honey Teriyaki Glaze together.
# Whisk to blend well.
# Combine the salmon and the Glaze together.
# Heat up a skillet on medium-low heat.
# Add the oil.
# Pan-fry the salmon on both sides until it's completely cooked inside and the glaze thickens.
# Garnish with sesame.

title: Cajun spiced fish tacos
text:
!! About

Fish tacos are one of those dishes that converted skeptics on first bite. The Baja-style version — battered, fried, sauced — gets all the press, but a quick spice-rubbed fish in a soft tortilla, dressed with avocado, lettuce, and salsa, is arguably better and definitely faster.

This recipe leans into Cajun spice and cayenne, which gives the fish a peppery edge that wakes up the cool toppings. Sour cream cools it down, lemon brightens it up, and the whole thing comes together in about fifteen minutes. Summer food, even if it isn't summer.

!! Ingredients

* 2 tbsp [[cajun]]
* 1 tsp [[cayenne pepper]]
* 4 fillets [[white fish]]
* 1 tsp [[vegetable oil]]
* 8 [[flour tortilla]]
* 1 sliced [[avocado]]
* 2 shredded [[little gem lettuce]]
* 4 shredded [[Spring Onions]]
* 1 x 300ml [[salsa]]
* 1 pot [[sour cream]]
* 1 [[lemon]]
* 1 clove finely chopped [[garlic]]

!! Steps

# On a large plate, mix the cajun spice and cayenne pepper with a little seasoning and use to coat the fish all over.
# Heat a little oil in a frying pan, add in the fish and cook over a medium heat until golden. Cook in batches if you don't have enough room in the pan.
# Reduce the heat and continue frying until the fish is cooked through, about 10 minutes.
# Meanwhile, prepare the dressing by combining all the ingredients with a little seasoning.
# Soften the tortillas by heating in the microwave for 5-10 seconds.
# Pile high with the avocado, lettuce and spring onion, add a spoonful of salsa, top with large flakes of fish and drizzle over the dressing.

title: Portuguese fish stew (Caldeirada de peixe)
text:
!! About

//Caldeirada// is the Portuguese answer to the question every coastal cuisine eventually asks: //what do we do with everything in the catch?// The answer, in this case, is ''all of it'' — cod, squid, prawns, clams, mussels — into one pot with onion, pepper, white wine, saffron, and potatoes, simmered until everything is tender and the broth is fragrant.

It is a generous, communal dish, meant for the middle of a table with bread for soaking. Don't stir it too aggressively once the seafood is in — let the layers settle and respect each other. Serve with the toasted baguette and let everyone build their own bowl.

!! Ingredients

* 2 finely chopped [[Onions]]
* 1 Diced [[Red Pepper]]
* Small bunch [[Coriander]]
* 1 small [[Red Chilli]]
* 3 cloves [[Garlic]]
* 400ml [[Dry White Wine]]
* Pinch [[Saffron]]
* 1 [[Bay Leaf]]
* 300g [[Potatoes]]
* 400g [[Plum Tomatoes]]
* 600g [[Cod]]
* 300g [[Squid]]
* 8 [[Tiger Prawns]]
* 500g [[Clams]]
* 500g [[Mussels]]
* 1 sliced [[Baguette]]

!! Steps

# Heat a drizzle of oil in a large, deep-sided frying pan, and fry the onion and pepper on a medium heat until softened but not browned.
# Finely chop the coriander stalks (keep the leaves for later), and add to the pan with the chilli and chopped garlic.
# Fry for another few minutes.
# Add the wine, saffron and bay leaf and let it simmer until reduced by half.
# Add the potatoes, tomatoes, and 300ml water and bring to a gentle boil.
# Break up the tomatoes with a spoon on the side of the pan and simmer for 20-25 minutes until the potatoes are just tender, and the tomatoes have broken down.
# Season well, then gently push the fish into the sauce, and arrange the squid, prawns, clams and mussels on the surface.
# Put the lid on and cook for 6-8 minutes until the mussel and clam shells have opened, the prawns are cooked and the fish is flaky.
# Toast the bread, rub lightly with the halved garlic clove and drizzle with olive oil.

title: Callaloo and SaltFish
text:
!! About

//Callaloo// is both a leafy green (similar to amaranth or taro leaves, depending on the island) and the Caribbean dish made with it. Pairing it with salt fish — typically cod, soaked overnight to draw out the salt — produces one of the great Jamaican breakfasts and a plate that's been on the island for centuries, going back to West African cooking traditions carried across the Atlantic.

Bacon, scotch bonnet, thyme, and tomatoes round it out. Eat with hard-dough bread, fried dumplings, or boiled green bananas. Heat is essential — don't skip the scotch bonnet, but mind your fingers when you chop it.

!! Ingredients

* 1/2 lb [[Salt Cod]]
* 4 [[Bacon]]
* 525g [[Callaloo]]
* 1 chopped [[Onion]]
* 2 chopped [[Spring Onions]]
* 2 cloves minced [[Garlic]]
* 1 chopped [[Scotch Bonnet]]
* 2 chopped [[Plum Tomatoes]]
* 2 sprigs [[Thyme]]
* 1/4 tsp [[Black Pepper]]

!! Steps

# Soak salted fish in water overnight.
# Heat salted fish in water on stove until water boils.
# Remove from heat and drain.
# Shred salted fish once it cools.
# Cook bacon in skillet over medium heat until crispy.
# Remove bacon from heat and drain the majority of the bacon grease, leaving about 1 tablespoon in the skillet.
# Add yellow onion, green onion, scotch bonnet pepper, and garlic to the skillet and stir.
# Cook for about 2 minutes or until onions soften.
# Add salted fish to skillet and stir.
# Cook for about a minute.
# Add callaloo, roma tomatoes, thyme, and black pepper.
# Stir to combine and cook until heated through, about 2 minutes.

title: Provençal Omelette Cake
text:
!! About

A //gâteau d'omelettes// is a sort of Provençal showpiece: thin omelettes stacked into a cake, each layer flavored differently — courgette and spring onion in one, roasted red pepper and chili in another — and bound with herbed cream cheese between the layers. Sliced into wedges, it reveals stripes like a savory layer cake.

It takes some patience. Each omelette has to be cooked carefully and cooled before stacking. But the result is genuinely beautiful and wonderfully suited to a brunch table or a warm-day lunch with rocket and shaved parmesan on top.

!! Ingredients

* 10 [[Eggs]]
* 1 tbs [[Olive Oil]]
* 2 finely chopped [[Courgettes]]
* 3 finely chopped [[Spring Onions]]
* 4 [[Red Pepper]]
* 1 clove peeled crushed [[Garlic Clove]]
* 1 [[Red Chilli]]
* 300g [[Cream Cheese]]
* 6 tblsp [[Milk]]
* 4 tbs [[Chives]]
* 2 tbs [[Basil]]
* to serve [[Rocket]]
* to serve [[Parmesan]]

!! Steps

```
# Break the eggs into two bowls, five in each.
# Whisk lightly and season with salt and pepper.
# Heat the oil in a pan, add the courgettes and spring onions, then fry gently for about 10 mins until softened.
# Cool the courgette mixture.
# Stir into one bowl of eggs with a little salt and pepper.
# Add the roasted peppers to the other bowl of eggs with the garlic, chilli, salt and pepper.
# Heat a little oil in a 20-23cm frying pan, preferably non-stick.
# Pour the eggs with courgette into a measuring jug.
# Pour about one-third of the mixture into the pan, swirling it to cover the base of the pan.
# Cook until the egg is set and lightly browned underneath.
# Cover the pan with a plate and invert the omelette onto it.
# Slide it back into the pan to cook the other side.
# Repeat with the remaining mix to make two more omelettes, adding a little oil to the pan each time.
# Stack the omelettes onto a plate.
# Make three omelettes in the same way with the red pepper mixture.
# Stack them on a separate plate.
# Beat the cheese to soften it, then beat in the milk to make a spreadable consistency.
# Stir in the herbs, salt and pepper.
# Line a deep, 20-23cm round cake tin with cling film (use a tin the same size as the frying pan).
# Select the best red pepper omelette and place in the tin, prettiest side down.
# Spread with a thin layer of cheese filling, then cover with a courgette omelette.
# Repeat, alternating the layers, until all the omelettes and filling are in the tin, finishing with an omelette.
# Flip the cling film over the omelette.
# Chill for up to 24 hrs.
```

title: Salmon Eggs Eggs Benedict
text:
!! About

Eggs Benedict is one of the great American breakfast inventions, and there's an enduring debate over whether the smoked salmon variation should be called Benedict, Royale, or Hemingway. (The British tend to say //Royale//, the Americans tend to say //Florentine// if there's spinach involved, and nobody has actually settled the salmon question.)

What matters is the assembly: a toasted English muffin, smoked salmon, a perfectly poached egg, a generous spoonful of warm hollandaise. The hollandaise is the part people fear, but it's just egg yolks, butter, and lemon, whisked patiently over gentle heat. Make it once and the mystery is gone forever.

!! Ingredients

* 4 [[Eggs]]
* 2 tbs [[White Wine Vinegar]]
* 2 [[English Muffins]]
* To serve [[Butter]]
* 8 slices [[Smoked Salmon]]
* 2 tsp [[Lemon Juice]]
* 2 tsp [[White Wine Vinegar]]
* 3 Yolkes [[Egg]]
* 125g [[Unsalted Butter]]

!! Steps

# Make the Hollandaise sauce first. Put the lemon juice and vinegar in a small bowl, add the egg yolks and whisk with a balloon whisk until light and frothy.
# Place the bowl over a pan of simmering water and whisk until the mixture thickens.
# Gradually add the butter, whisking constantly until thick – if it looks like it might be splitting, whisk off the heat for a few mins.
# Season and keep warm.
# Bring a large pan of water to the boil and add the vinegar.
# Lower the heat so that the water is simmering gently.
# Stir the water so you have a slight whirlpool, then slide in the eggs one by one.
# Cook each egg for about 4 mins, then remove with a slotted spoon.
# Lightly toast and butter the muffins.
# Put a couple of slices of salmon on each muffin half.
# Top each with an egg and spoon over some Hollandaise.
# Garnish with chopped chives.

title: Roast aubergine with goat's cheese & toasted flatbread (photo)
Roast aubergine with goat's cheese & toasted flatbread
photo: Roast aubergine with goat's cheese & toasted flatbread (photo)
text:
!! About

A meze-adjacent plate that punches well above its ingredient list: aubergine slices roasted until silken, cherry tomatoes blistered alongside, pita torn and crisped in the same oven. It all gets dressed with a punchy mint-shallot-chili vinaigrette and finished with crumbled goat's cheese and rocket.

Eat it warm, ideally outside, ideally with someone who will appreciate that you fanned the aubergine slices artfully on the plate. Equally happy as a starter or a light main with bread.

!! Ingredients

* 2 sliced [[Aubergine]]
* 3  tablespoons [[Extra Virgin Olive Oil]]
* 12 [[Cherry Tomatoes]]
* 1 [[Pita Bread]]
* 3  tablespoons [[Balsamic Vinegar]]
* Handful [[Mint]]
* 1 chopped [[Shallots]]
* 1 sliced [[Shallots]]
* 1 chopped [[Red Chilli]]
* 50g [[Goats Cheese]]
* Handful [[Rocket]]

!! Steps

# Heat oven to 200C/180C fan/gas 6.
# Brush the aubergine slices with 1 tbsp of the oil, then season.
# Arrange on a baking tray or sheet and roast for 20 mins until browned, popping the tomatoes on the tray for the final 5 mins.
# Tear the flatbread into pieces and place on a separate baking sheet.
# Brown in the oven for 8 mins, or until crisp, then remove.
# For the dressing, in a small bowl, mix the vinegar, mint, chopped shallots, chilli, remaining oil and some salt and pepper.
# Scatter the aubergine slices, tomatoes, sliced shallot and crisp flatbread into a serving bowl.
# Pour over the dressing, sprinkle with the goat's cheese and scatter over a little rocket.

title: Beef and Mustard Pie
text:
!! About

The British pie is its own small universe — steak and kidney, pork, fish, shepherd's, cottage — and at the savory end, beef-and-mustard pie is a classic of pub kitchens and Sunday tables alike. Slow-cooked beef in red wine and stock, sharpened with grain mustard and topped with golden puff pastry that shatters under the spoon.

This is a project rather than a weeknight dinner — the filling needs hours on a low heat to break down properly — but most of that time is unattended. Make the filling a day ahead; it improves overnight. Serve with green beans and a heap of mashed potatoes.

!! Ingredients

* 1kg [[Beef]]
* 2 tbs [[Plain Flour]]
* 2 tbs [[Rapeseed Oil]]
* 200ml [[Red Wine]]
* 400ml [[Beef Stock]]
* 1 finely sliced [[Onion]]
* 2 chopped [[Carrots]]
* 3 sprigs [[Thyme]]
* 2 tbs [[Mustard]]
* 2 free-range [[Egg Yolks]]
* 400g [[Puff Pastry]]
* 300g [[Green Beans]]
* 25g [[Butter]]
* pinch [[Salt]]
* pinch [[Pepper]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 150C/300F/Gas 2.
# Toss the beef and flour together in a bowl with some salt and black pepper.
# Heat a large casserole until hot, add half of the rapeseed oil and enough of the beef to just cover the bottom of the casserole.
# Fry until browned on each side, then remove and set aside.
# Repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
# Return the beef to the pan, add the wine and cook until the volume of liquid has reduced by half.
# Add the stock, onion, carrots, thyme and mustard, and season well with salt and pepper.
# Cover with a lid and place in the oven for two hours.
# Remove from the oven, check the seasoning and set aside to cool.
# Remove the thyme.
# When the beef is cool and you're ready to assemble the pie, preheat the oven to 200C/400F/Gas 6.
# Transfer the beef to a pie dish, brush the rim with the beaten egg yolks and lay the pastry over the top.
# Brush the top of the pastry with more beaten egg.
# Trim the pastry so there is just enough excess to crimp the edges.
# Place in the oven and bake for 30 minutes, or until the pastry is golden-brown and cooked through.
# Bring a saucepan of salted water to the boil, add the beans and cook for 4-5 minutes, or until just tender.
# Drain and toss with the butter.
# Season with black pepper.

title: Beef Lo Mein
text:
!! About

//Lo mein// — //tossed noodles// — is the Cantonese-American take on a classic stir-fry-with-noodles formula, and it's been a staple of Chinese takeout in the West for nearly a century. The version most of us grew up with is glossy, garlicky, slightly sweet, packed with vegetables and a bit of meat.

This recipe walks through the proper home version: marinate the beef briefly with cornstarch and sesame oil so it stays tender, parboil the noodles just barely, then everything goes into the wok at high heat and comes together in minutes. Oyster sauce is the unifying flavor. Don't skip it.

!! Ingredients

* 1/2 lb [[Beef]]
* pinch [[Salt]]
* pinch [[Pepper]]
* 2 tsp [[Sesame Seed Oil]]
* 1/2 [[Egg]]
* 3 tbs [[Starch]]
* 5 tbs [[Oil]]
* 1/4 lb [[Noodles]]
* 1/2 cup [[Onion]]
* 1 tsp [[Minced Garlic]]
* 1 tsp [[Ginger]]
* 1 cup [[Bean Sprouts]]
* 1 cup [[Mushrooms]]
* 1 cup [[Water]]
* 1 tbs [[Oyster Sauce]]
* 1 tsp [[Sugar]]
* 1 tsp [[Soy Sauce]]

!! Steps

# In a bowl, combine the beef, salt, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, 1/2 egg, corn starch, and 1 tablespoon of oil and mix together.
# In a 6 qt pot, add the noodles to boiling water until submerged and boil on high heat for 10 seconds.
# Strain the noodles and cool with cold water.
# Add 2 tablespoons of oil and the beef to a wok and cook on high heat until beef is medium cooked.
# Set the cooked beef aside.
# Add 2 tablespoons of oil, onions, minced garlic, minced ginger, bean sprouts, mushrooms, and peapods to the wok with 1.5 cups of water, or until the vegetables are submerged.
# Add the noodles to the wok.
# Add oyster sauce, 1 pinch white pepper, 1 teaspoon sesame seed oil, sugar, and 1 teaspoon of soy sauce.
# Add the beef to the wok and stir-fry.

title: Cassava pizza
text:
!! About

//Casabe// — a flatbread made from grated, pressed, and toasted bitter cassava — is one of the oldest foods of the Americas, predating European contact by thousands of years. The Taíno made it, and Venezuelans and other Caribbean populations still do. It's traditionally eaten as a cracker-like bread with stews and beans.

This recipe takes that ancient flatbread and turns it into a pizza base — tomato sauce, mozzarella, chorizo, turkey ham, sweetcorn, olives, peppers — baked just long enough to melt the cheese. It's a clever, resourceful, slightly unexpected use of a very old ingredient. Crispy, savory, and on the table in fifteen minutes.

!! Ingredients

* 6 cut thick slices [[Casabe]]
* 450g [[Tomato Sauce]]
* 225g [[Chorizo]]
* 225g [[Turkey Ham]]
* 75g [[Sweetcorn]]
* 40g [[Green Olives]]
* 55g [[Paprika]]
* 50g [[Mozzarella]]

!! Steps

# Preheat the oven to 200ºC.
# Cut the bacon or chorizo into medium pieces and the paprika into strips.
# Spread a little tomato sauce and mozzarella cheese on each portion of cassava.
# Add the bacon or chorizo, corn, turkey ham, some olives and paprika.
# Bake for 7 to 10 minutes.
